messages:
Micah: quick follow-up from the RFC review: we still haven't agreed on whether the runtime should coerce QKV layouts to the kernel-preferred order (force-copy) or rely on per-kernel adapters that accept multiple strides.

Sanjay: leaning toward adapters. copies kill perf on short sequences. even a single memcpy per request is expensive at 1k qps.

Olivia: adapters are nicer for forward-compatibility, but they complicate kernel selector. we end up with 3x more code paths and test permutations.

Aisha: question - how often do we see non-contiguous QKV in client workloads vs something we control (model repo)? if it's rare, maybe we copy for the rare case and keep kernels lean.

Tomas: it's common in our dedicated fleet where customers deploy fused HF checkpoints that store QKV planar. We can't force customers to re-ship weights.

Micah: agreed. customer-run models are a big factor. proposal: keep contiguous-contiguous kernels as primary path, add a tiny 'stride fallback' kernel that handles arbitrary ld/stride without full reordering. that kernel will be slower but avoids memcpy.

Sanjay: idea: small fallback kernel that does elementwise gather with vectorized loads - minimal buffer pressure. avoids full re-layout but still faster than memcpy+kernel.

Olivia: that approach still needs per-head vs per-token iteration order decisions. we've seen head-major loops that thrash cache for large-head models.

Micah: yes - here's a sketch of selector heuristic we discussed:

``
selector(cfg):
  if cfg.layout == CONTIG && cfg.heads <= 32 && seq <= 512:
    choose = fast_fused_kernel
  elif cfg.layout == PLANAR && hw_supports_gather:
    choose = stride_fallback_kernel
  else:
    if expected_qps_high and mem_bandwidth_limited:
      choose = memcpy_then_contig_kernel
    else:
      choose = generic_block_kernel
``

Aisha: can runtime probe hw_supports_gather? some GPUs have efficient byte/strided loads via ldg or PTX intrinsics.

Tomas: we can probe once at startup with a microbenchmark. add an env flag to override for experiments.

Olivia: runtime needs metrics: count of layout conversions, time spent in fallback kernel, memcpy time. otherwise we'll never know.

Sanjay: also track sequence-length distribution and head count per model; that will let selector adapt over time.

Micah: operational note: must preserve KV cache layout for incremental decoding. the fallback path must write back into the KV cache in the canonical contiguous format to avoid cascade conversion.

Aisha: good catch. that implies if we run stride_fallback on first token, we should materialize contig into cache for subsequent tokens.

Tomas: simple rule: fallback never mutates source weights - only materialize cache writes. avoids surprises when same weights are reused across requests.

Olivia: test plan: unit test correctness with random stride combinations, perf bench on sequences [8,32,128,512,2048], and integration with canary model in staging.

Micah: can we get a prototype of stride_fallback_kernel by EOW? Sanjay + Tomas pair?

Sanjay: yes, will prototype. will post microbench numbers here.

runtime-bot: deploy-check: new branch builds: qkv-layout-adapter/prototype - CI passed for x86, failed on aarch64 due to alignment assumptions.

Olivia: note the aarch64 failure - likely from unaligned vector loads in fallback. add tests for unaligned cases.

Sanjay: will fix. thanks.

Micah: thanks all. next steps: (1) prototype fallback kernel (Sanjay/Tomas), (2) implement selector config and startup probe (Olivia), (3) add metrics and cache-materialization rules (Aisha). We'll reconvene next Tuesday.

Aisha: ack :thumbsup:

Tomas: ack

Olivia: ack

Sanjay: ack
